By on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80346456/
1  ORDER

This Criminal Original Petition has been filed to quash the final report filed against the petitioners in Spl.S.C.No.25 of 2021, for the offences under Sections 3(1)(r), 3(1)(s), 3(2)(v), 3(1)(w)(i) of SC/ST (PoA) Amendment Act, 2015, Sections 355 and 376(1) of IPC, on the file of the learned Principal District Judge, Erode, on the ground of compromise.
2. The allegations in the final report is that the de facto complainant belongs to Scheduled Caste community.
The first petitioner under the pretext of marrying the de facto complainant, had sexual intercourse with her and thereafter, refused to marry her.
When the de facto complainant informed the same to the second petitioner who is the mother of the first petitioner, the second petitioner, in a public view, abused her by mentioning her caste name.
Hence, the case.

3. The learned counsel for the petitioners would submit the matter has been compromised between the parties and the de facto complainant has no objection in quashing the criminal proceedings against the petitioners and she has also filed an affidavit to that effect.
4. The learned counsel appearing for the respondent/de facto complainant would submit that due to misunderstanding and misconception, the de facto complainant has lodged the complaint.

Now the matter has been https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 24/11/2025 01:45:03 pm )
compromised between the parties and the de facto complainant is not willing to proceed with the criminal case as against the petitioners.
5.

The petitioners and the de facto complainant were present before this Court at the time of hearing and they were identified by the learned counsel for the petitioners and by Ms.D.Vasugi, WHC713,
AWPS, Erode.
6. This Court also enquired both the parties.

The de facto complainant admitted that due to misunderstanding and mistake of belief, she lodged the complaint and now, she has no objection in quashing the proceedings against the petitioners.
7.
This Court is satisfied that the parties have come to an amicable settlement between themselves.

8. The learned Government Advocate (Crl. Side) appearing on behalf of the respondent-Police submitted that though the parties entered into a compromise while this case is pending, this Court,
taking into account the seriousness of the offence, has to consider the issue as to whether an offence of this nature can be quashed on the ground of compromise between parties.
9. The main issue that requires the consideration of this Court is as to whether this Court can quash the criminal proceedings involving non- compoundable offences pending against the petitioners.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parbathbhai Aahir @ Parbathbhai
Vs. State https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

( Uploaded on: 24/11/2025 01:45:03 pm ) of Gujrat, reported in 2017 9 SCC 641 and in case of The State of Madhya Pradesh Vs. Dhruv Gurjar and Another reported in (2019) 2 MLJ Crl 10, has given sufficient guidelines that must be taken into consideration by this J.Praveenkumar vs The State Rep.

entities.text: State of Madhya Pradesh Vs. Dhruv Gurjar and Another reported in (2019) 2 MLJ Crl 10
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
By on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80346456/
2 Court while exercising its jurisdiction under Section 482 of Cr.P.C./528 BNSS, to quash non-compoundable offences.

One very important test that has been laid down is that the Court must necessarily examine if the crime in question is purely individual in nature or a crime against the society with overriding public interest.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that offences against the society with overriding public interest even if it gets settled between the parties, cannot be quashed by this Court.
10. In the present case, the offences in question are purely individual/personal in nature.

It involves dispute between the petitioners and the de facto complainant and quashing the proceedings, will not affect any overriding public interest in this case and no useful purpose will be served in continuing with the criminal proceedings.
11.

In view of the above, this Court is inclined to quash the proceedings against the petitioners in Spl.S.C.No.25 of 2021, on the file of the learned Principal District Judge, Erode, in exercise of its jurisdiction under Section 482 of Cr.P.C./528 BNSS.
12.
Accordingly, this Criminal Original Petition is allowed and the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

( Uploaded on: 24/11/2025 01:45:03 pm ) proceedings against the petitioners in Spl.S.C.No.25 of 2021, on the file of the learned Principal District Judge, Erode, is quashed subject to condition that the petitioners shall pay costs of Rs.15,000/- (Rupees Fifteen Thousand Only) jointly, to the credit of Tamil Nadu State Legal Services Authority, on or before 05.12.2025.
